paper.paper_scope: Experimental study of the deformation behaviour (yield stress, ductility, hardness, dislocation structure) of binary Fe-Al alloys with 0-18 at.% Al in monocrystalline and polycrystalline form, at room temperature and -100 °C, focusing on the effects of Al content and of quenching/annealing heat treatments (short-range ordering and quenched-in excess vacancies).

unmapped_findings: The paper reports that only heat treatments at temperatures above 600 °C significantly affect the mechanical behaviour of Fe-Al alloys, whereas short-range ordering (controlled by treatments below 600 °C) has no major impact on deformation behaviour.

A linear increase of yield stress with Al content was observed for polycrystalline Fe-Al alloys up to 18 at.% Al (hardening coefficient about 2.2 GPa), attributed to Suzuki's theory of solid-solution hardening, which contrasts with an earlier reported coefficient of ~1 GPa for monocrystals.

Quenching from 1100 °C traps excess vacancies that contribute to hardening/embrittlement and heal out only slowly (reported to heal at 300-400 °C, but the 300 °C/14 d anneal was insufficient for complete elimination).

Deformation twinning was observed at room temperature only for Fe-18%Al and at -100 °C for Al contents of 11-18%; yield stress drops at -100 °C occurred only for Fe-4%Al and Fe-6%Al and are tentatively attributed to interaction of mobile dislocations with vacancies.

Ordering reactions, the K-state (complex short-range ordering) and the related activation energy (~0.3 eV/atom, highest ordering at 250 °C) were characterised in separate studies (refs [16,20]) and are only summarised here.

The pure iron used for the aluminium-free reference was prepared by electron-beam remelting, whereas the Fe-Al alloys were prepared by vacuum induction melting (and, for selected alloys, levitation melting).
